```{r}
library(tidyverse)
cafe <-read.csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2026/2026-09-08/cafe.csv')
cappuccino_index =read.csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2026/2026-09-08/cappuccino_index.csv')
coffee_data<-cappuccino_index|>
  inner_join(cafe,join_by(country))
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
West_Richland<-USA_complete|>
filter(city=="West Richland")
#graph1
#price vs hourly wage for USA
USA_coffee_data<-coffee_data|>
  filter(country=="USA")
USA_coffee_data|>
  ggplot(aes(x=hourly_wage_gbp,y=price_gbp))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")

#graph3
#graph for all the countries
coffee_data|>
  ggplot(aes(x=hourly_wage_gbp,y=price_gbp))+
  geom_point()+

#graph2
ggplot(USA_complete,
       aes(x = hourly_wage, y = price_gbp)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(data =West_Richland,colour = "green")+
  geom_text(data = West_Richland,label = "West_Richland",size = 3,vjust = 1.9)+
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "darkred") +
  labs(
    title = "The cappuccino_index Index of coffee in USA",
    subtitle = "Higher coffee prices are weakly associated with higher wages,with West Richland standing out for its  high price",
    x = "Hourly wage ",
    y = "Cappuccino price ",
    alt="A graph of hourly wage against the price_gbp in british pounds",
    caption = "Source: Week2 TidyTuesday|created by Apiu|Date:10/09/26"
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_dollar(prefix = "£"))+

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = -0.1,size = 6)
    
  )
```

Background
-The coffee_data is a data set formed from joining two data sets coffee data and cappucino index.The coffee data consists  variable such as coffee prices,wages,countries,hourly wage,whether the cafes are in urban or not.
-The Capuccino index on the other hand is a data set that contains the country and how long it would take a person to work in a cafe to obtain a cup of cappucino.
-Based on the visualisations  above The United States seems to have  the largest number of coffee shops hence my interest in what impact does the hourly wages have on coffee prices in the USA.

**Research question**

#How are the coffee prices associated with the hourly wage in the Unites States
There appears to be a weak  positive linear relationship between the price to get a cup of coffee in the united states and the hourly wage suggesting that there are other possible factors affecting this relationship that could be location. 

There appears to be a weak positive linear relationship between hourly wages and coffee prices in the United States. This suggests that places with higher hourly wages tend to have slightly higher coffee prices. However, hourly wage alone explains only about 4.41% of the variation in coffee prices. Other factors, such as location, may also help explain differences in coffee prices
